'''Peter John Goodhew''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|CBE|FREng}} (born 3 July 1943, in London)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pcwww.liv.ac.uk/~goodhew/biography.html|title=Professor Peter J Goodhew FREng|first=Peter|last=Goodhew|website=pcwww.liv.ac.uk}}</ref> is an [[Electron microscopy|electron microscopist]] who has published extensively on metallic and [[Semiconductor|semiconducting]] materials and has authored or co-authored several widely used books on transmission (and scanning transmission) electron microscopy.<ref>''Thin foil preparation for electron microscopy'', P J Goodhew. 2nd edition North Holland, 1985 {{ISBN|0-444-80699-7}}</ref><ref>''Electron microscopy and analysis'' 3rd edition P J Goodhew, F J Humphreys and R Beanland, Taylor & Francis, 2001 {{ISBN|0-7484-0968-8}}</ref><ref>''Specimen Preparation for TEM of Materials'', P J Goodhew, Royal Microscopical Society (Oxford U Press) 1984 {{ISBN|0-19-856403-1}}</ref><ref>''An Introduction to Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy'', R J Keyse, A J Garratt-Reed, P J Goodhew & G W Lorimer, 1998; BIOS {{ISBN|1-85996-066-9}}</ref> He was the leader of the UK [[SuperSTEM]] project at the [[STFC Daresbury Laboratory]] for ten years and has been Dean of Engineering and Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the [[University of Liverpool]].

During his career at the Universities of [[University of Surrey|Surrey]] and Liverpool he established the MATTER [[computer-based learning]] project and was the founding Director of the [[UK Centre for Materials Education]] (UKCME), one of the Subject Centres of the [[Higher Education Academy]].

Goodhew was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[2017 New Year Honours]] for services to Engineering and Education.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=61803|supp=y|page=N9|date=31 December 2016}}</ref>

==Books==
Goodhew is the author of the 2010 book ''Teaching Engineering'', published by [[UKCME]].<ref>''Teaching Engineering'', P. J. Goodhew, 2010; UKCME {{ISBN|978-1-907207-22-8}}</ref>
